promptLatex: What is the minimum number of integers that must be selected from {1, 2, ..., 30} to guarantee that at least one pair has a sum of 31?
hintLatex: Group the numbers into pairs that sum to $31$ and treat those pairs as boxes.
The pairs $(1,30), (2,29), \ldots, (15,16)$ are $15$ boxes, and taking one number from each box avoids any pair summing to $31$.
So $15$ numbers can still avoid a sum of $31$, while any $16$ numbers fill one box completely by the pigeonhole principle.
solutionLatex:
Pair $1$ through $30$ into the $15$ pairs that sum to $31$: $(1,30), (2,29), \ldots, (15,16)$. Those $15$ pairs are the pigeonholes.

Selecting $15$ numbers, one from each pair, produces no pair summing to $31$, so $15$ is not enough.

Selecting $16$ numbers puts $16$ pigeons in $15$ holes, so one pair is selected in full, and a full pair sums to $31$.

The minimum is therefore $16$.
